# Card Block API — llms.txt

Card Block API is an open, machine-readable directory of how to block a lost or stolen payment instrument (debit card, credit card, UPI) at any Indian bank. Pilot scope: India. Goal: universal.

## What this is

- A static JSON data layer: one file per bank, plus an index. Hosted on GitHub Pages, versioned in git.
- Every blocking method carries `confidence`, `last_verified`, `sources`, and `confirmations` so agents and humans can judge freshness before acting.
- Data changes only through pull requests — the git history is the audit trail.

## What this is not

- Not a blocking service. This API cannot block your card; it tells you exactly how to do it through the bank's official channels.
- Not a UI project. Websites, MCP servers, and apps are derived surfaces built on top of this data, maintained elsewhere.

## Endpoints

- GET /data/index.json — API manifest: version, endpoint map, bank count, freshness aggregate, channel list.
- GET /data/banks/index.json — summary of all banks (slug, name, type, card_types, method_count, verification_status, last_verified, freshness bands).
- GET /data/banks/{slug}.json — full blocking data for one bank. Slug list from the index.
- GET /schemas/bank.schema.json — JSON Schema (draft 2020-12) for per-bank files.
- GET /schemas/index.schema.json — JSON Schema for the bank index.

## Freshness semantics

Computed client-side from `last_verified` (ISO date):

- fresh: verified within 30 days
- aging: 31–90 days
- stale: over 90 days

Treat `stale` as "verify through a second source before relying on this". The index carries a pre-computed `freshness` aggregate: `{ fresh, aging, stale }`.

## Verification status ladder

`human_verified` > `agent_verified` > `unverified` > `disputed` (suppressed pending re-verification).

## Reporting a correction

Reports go through GitHub issues (transport layer; see docs/API.md for the flow). A report never mutates data directly — it flags the bank `needs_reverify` and the data loop re-verifies and commits the change with fresh sources. Never include card numbers, PINs, OTPs, or passwords in a report.

## Versioning

- `schema_version` in /data/index.json follows semver. Patch: doc fixes. Minor: additive fields. Major: breaking field changes — clients should pin on minor and re-check the index before bulk reads.
